e-9357.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit Using the Limit Definition of Euler's Number
e-9357.worked_solution:
Recall the following special limit: 

$$
e = \lim_{n \to  \infty} \left(1+\dfrac{1}{n}\right)^{n}
$$

Now, we rewrite the given limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{3n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{[{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{n}]}^{3} \\  & ={[{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{n}]}^{3} \\  & ={e}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

e-9358.knowledge_point: Applying the Limit Definition of the Exponential Function
e-9358.worked_solution:
Recall the following special limit: 

$$
e^x = \lim_{n \to  \infty} \left(1+\dfrac{x}{n}\right)^{n}
$$

Now, we rewrite the given limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{x}{n})}^{-n/2} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{[{(1+\frac{x}{n})}^{n}]}^{-1/2} \\  & ={[{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{x}{n})}^{n}]}^{-1/2} \\  & ={({e}^{x})}^{-1/2} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{e}^{x}}}\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying the Limit Definition of the Exponential Function
content.worked_solution:
Recall the following special limit: 

$$
{e}^{u}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{u}{n})}^{n}
$$

Hence, with $u=\pi x$, we get

$$
{e}^{\pi x}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{\pi x}{n})}^{n}
$$

Now, we rewrite the given limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{\pi x}{n})}^{2n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{[{(1+\frac{\pi x}{n})}^{n}]}^{2} \\  & ={[{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{\pi x}{n})}^{n}]}^{2} \\  & ={({e}^{\pi x})}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2\pi x}\end{aligned}
$$
